subject: Cloud Marketplace & PO vs Card — procurement ops checklist and next steps
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@clearsky.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: procurement ops checklist — PO vs card vs marketplace

Hannah — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so your procurement/finops team can evaluate paths: 

1) Commercial paths we discussed
  - Direct (credit card or invoice to Redwood billing team) — fastest for pilots, requires billing contact and PO number for invoiced deals.
  - PO + standard invoicing (Net 30) — you flagged internal PO process and central finance approval; we need your PO template and any required GL/line-item fields.
  - AWS Marketplace (Private Offer / SaaS Contracts) — preferred by your platform team for procurement visibility; this adds a listing/POA step and longer lead time, but provides consolidated AWS billing.

2) Clarifying questions I promised to capture for your finops folks: 
  - Do you require PO number on the invoice for every renewal or only initial purchase?
  - If Marketplace: do you need product-level line items on the AWS invoice or is a consolidated SKU acceptable?
  - Any VAT/withholding tax nuances for your vendor setup?
  - Who signs commercial contracts at ClearSky (legal vs procurement)?

3) Operational items Redwood can provide now to accelerate evals:
  - Our standard PO template (attached) and sample invoice fields we populate.
  - Marketplace onboarding checklist (what AWS needs to accept private offers).
  - A short SOW for the pilot (if you need it to generate an internal PO).

Next steps (proposed):
  - Hannah: share the PO template and preferred billing contact (Priya?) by EOD Wed.
  - Markus/Marissa: we’ll confirm whether AWS marketplace private offer is supported for your region and timeline, and return a one-page billing mapping by Fri.
  - Karthik: I’ll loop you on technical entitlements in case marketplace listing requires SSO mapping.

Attachment: PO_template.pdf (pdf, 48KB)

Thanks — Markus
--
Markus Klein
Senior Sales Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@clearsky.io>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Bennett <tom.bennett@clearsky.io>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@clearsky.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: procurement ops checklist — PO vs card vs marketplace

Markus — thanks for the crisp recap. A few answers and clarifications from our side: 

- PO process: Our procurement team requires a PO for all commercial purchases over $5k. For pilot projects under $5k they allow card, but our policy is shifting toward PO-first for visibility.
- Billing fields: We do need a PO number and AP contact on the invoice. Ideally the invoice has project code and GL code in separate fields (we can annotate the PO template).
- Marketplace: our Cloud Platform prefers AWS Marketplace (private offers) since it keeps costs on the same vendor bill and simplifies chargeback. However, Marketplace listing needs sign-off from Cloud Ops and takes ~2–3 weeks for private offer setup.
- Legal: Commercial agreements are routed to Legal, but Procurement initiates PO requests — final signature by Legal.

I’m attaching our RFP Q&A (excerpt) to show expected vendor info. We can share the PO template and GL codes by tomorrow.

Main ask: can Redwood provide a one-page mapping (your invoice fields -> our PO fields) and confirm whether you accept private offers on the AWS Marketplace and if any reseller entitlements are required? Also include estimated timeline for Marketplace private offer activation.

Attachment: Clearsky_RFP_QA.xlsx (xlsx, 12KB)

Appreciate it,
Hannah
Procurement Manager | ClearSky Analytics
hannah.lee@clearsky.io
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@clearsky.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: procurement ops checklist — PO vs card vs marketplace

Hannah — thanks, got the RFP Q&A. Quick answers below and an attached one-page mapping for your procurement/finance team. 

- Marketplace support: Yes — Redwood supports AWS Marketplace private offers for US customers. We can route through Marketplace so ClearSky is billed by AWS; private offer setup typically takes 7–18 business days depending on AWS review and legal signoffs. If you need faster start, we can do an initial pilot on card/invoice and migrate to Marketplace for scale.
- Invoice fields: see attached mapping (we included example values for project code and GL lines). We accept PO numbers on invoices and can place PO in the invoice header as required.
- Reseller entitlements: Not required for standard private offers; if you have an MSSP/reseller involved, we’ll need to confirm the AWS partner ARN.
- Tax/withholding: Please have Priya confirm whether ClearSky requires any withholding tax documentation — Redwood can produce W-9 and our standard tax forms.

Next steps: 
  1) Hannah/Priya: send PO template and GL codes by EOD Thu so we can populate sample invoice.
  2) Redwood: we’ll produce sample invoice and start Marketplace private offer intake once we have signed commercial terms.
  3) Marissa/Karthik: we’ll prepare the Marketplace onboarding checklist and technical entitlement notes.

Attachment: invoice_field_mapping.pdf (pdf, 24KB)

If helpful, Karthik and I can join a 20-minute call with Procurement to walk through the mapping and timeline.

Best — Markus
--
Markus Klein
Senior Sales Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Tom Bennett <tom.bennett@clearsky.io>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@clearsky.io>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@clearsky.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: procurement ops checklist — PO vs card vs marketplace

Markus/Team — brief internal update from procurement: we ran your invoice mapping by finance and they’re happy with the fields. Two items before we can issue a formal PO: 

1) A short confirmation from Legal that Redwood’s standard T&Cs will be acceptable or a redline set we should expect.
2) Confirmation of estimated Marketplace activation lead time in business days if we proceed with private offer (we are targeting a production pilot in early June).

If you can send an expected turn time for private offers (business days) and a pointer to the contract we should circulate to Legal, we’ll lock dates and share a PO by next Tue. Otherwise, we’ll start the pilot via card and invoice and migrate to Marketplace afterward.

Thanks — Tom
Head of Cloud Platform | ClearSky Analytics
